article_title: Tesla Launches Robotaxi in Miami, Its First City Outside Texas and California, But Maps Only a Small Geofenced Zone

content_preview.title: Tesla Launches Robotaxi in Miami, Its First City Outside Texas and California, But Maps Only a Small Geofenced Zone
content_preview.summary: Tesla began robotaxi service in Miami on July 3, 2026 - its first city outside Texas and California - but the geofence covers only a small slice of Miami-Dade even as its fleet shrinks.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Tesla expanded its robotaxi program to Miami, Florida, on July 3, 2026, marking the third state its autonomous ride-hailing platform has reached since launching the previous summer, according to [Teslarati](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-expands-robotaxi-florida-third-state-autonomy/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (477 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Sourcing is explicit and inline-attributed to the correct outlet for every claim.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three gzipped snapshots from sources/2026-07/tesla-launches-robotaxi-in-miami-its-first-city-outside-texas-and-california-but-maps-only-a-small-geofenced-zone/. source-0.html.gz (Teslarati, 'Tesla expands Robotaxi to Florida', July 3 2026, status 200): CONFIRMED the July 3 2026 Miami launch, 'third state ... since launching last Summer', the ~10-14 sq mi western/central Miami zone, the list of active locations (Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio in TX + Bay Area in CA), and the Waymo 'broader in eastern neighborhoods' comparison. source-1.html.gz (Electrek, 'Tesla maps a tiny Robotaxi zone in Miami', July 3 2026, status 200): CONFIRMED the geofence covering only a small slice of the metro, the SR-826/US-41 boundaries, 'mostly West Miami and a strip stretching toward Doral and Sweetwater', exclusion of downtown/Miami Beach/most of Coral Gables, the five-city 1H-2026 target list (Phoenix, Orlando, Tampa, Las Vegas), the June 2025 Austin launch, and the unsupervised-fleet decline from ~25 cumulative toward ~14 active cars. source-2.html.gz (TechCrunch, Dallas/Houston, April 18 2026, status 200): CONFIRMED that Tesla began offering rides without safety drivers in January 2026. All three domains are on config/source_allowlist.txt. The internal cross-reference (/article/2026-04/03-tesla-begins-cybercab...) resolves to an existing published article.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific number, boundary, date, and city name maps verbatim to a snapshot. The article correctly resolved the airport-inclusion source conflict by OMISSION: Teslarati's snapshot says the geofence includes Miami International Airport (MIA) while Electrek's says 'no airport' — the article makes no airport claim in either direction, which is the honest resolution. Verified that the two dropped details from the source-conflict process did not resurface: no NHTSA crash-figure quote and no bespoke 'no safety monitor' assertion appear in the body. The only safety-driver statement ('without human safety drivers in January 2026') is independently and correctly sourced to the accessible TechCrunch snapshot, not to a bot-blocked source. 'Most of Coral Gables' (article) is consistent with Electrek's 'only a corner of Coral Gables'.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The critical framing (small geofence, shrinking fleet, geography as the harder problem) is attributed to the cited outlets rather than editorialized, and the regulatory/safety framing is kept general ('regulatory scrutiny of its camera-based system') and anchored to prior Machine Herald coverage rather than to unsourced specifics.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Prior Tesla coverage (2026-04 Cybercab mass production) is a different angle and is cited as background; recent robotaxi articles concern Waymo and XPeng. No existing article covers the Miami launch.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE.
